title: Language-Assisted Image Clustering Guided by Discriminative Relational Signals and Adaptive Semantic Centers
claim: Prior methods' text features collapse into a compact, near-identical cluster, and fixed class-name centers misclassify, whereas learned relational features and centers discriminate better.
layout: 2 panels split by dashed line; left plots and heatmaps, right score tables
description: The figure has two panels separated by a vertical dashed line. Panel (a), on the left, has three parts. (i) is a 3D PCA scatter plot. A large orange cloud of image features sits apart from a tiny blue cluster of noun text features. A legend box sits below it. (ii) is a red-toned cosine-similarity heatmap in which almost every cell is uniformly high, showing that text features are near-identical across samples. (iii) is a blue-and-red heatmap with a strong diagonal and low off-diagonal values, showing better inter-class discriminability. Panel (b), on the right, shows three photos of watercraft and water sports. Below them, a blue table gives zero-shot CLIP scores for the class names Skijet, Surfing and Rafting, with a wrong score in red. A yellow table gives scores for learned centers S0 to S2, with the correct scores in green. A legend sits at the bottom.
caption: (a) Analysis of the phenomena in the first step of existing LAICs and our method on the ImageNet-10 dataset. (i) Jointly PCA results shows text features of noun from candidate set exhibit a more compact distribution, which are closed to each other compared to image features. (ii) Due to the phenomenon in (i), the similarity of text features across different samples are overall highly similar, leading to weak inter-class discriminability. (iii) Rows of our learned image-text representation matrix performs as new representation, showing better inter-class discriminability with in-class consistency retained. (b) Classification scores of three images (from DTD dataset) with respect to different semantic centers obtained by different methods. Zero-shot CLIP relies on semantic centers using ground-truth class names, which may not always capture accurate semantics (e.g, an image of motorboat is incorrectly assigned to "Surfing”. Our learned semantic center can be even better than class names, showing stronger discriminability.
abstract: Language-Assisted Image Clustering (LAIC) augments the input images with additional texts with the help of vision-language models (VLMs) to promote clustering performance. Despite recent progress, existing LAIC methods often overlook two issues: (i) textual features constructed for each image are highly similar, leading to weak inter-class discriminability; (ii) the clustering step is restricted to pre-built image-text alignments, limiting the potential for better utilization of the text modality. To address these issues, we propose a new LAIC framework with two complementary components. First, we exploit cross-modal relations to produce more discriminative self-supervision signals for clustering, as it compatible with most VLMs training mechanisms. Second, we learn category-wise continuous semantic centers via prompt learning to produce the final clustering assignments. Extensive experiments on eight benchmark datasets demonstrate that our method achieves an average improvement of 2.6% over state-of-the-art methods, and the learned semantic centers exhibit strong interpretability. Code is available in the supplementary material.
